title: Three-state Potts antiferromagnet on the 600-cell
statement: Colour the 120 vertices of the 600-cell {3,3,5} with three colours (a 3-state Potts spin on each vertex) and count the monochromatic edges among its 720 edges: this is the energy of the 3-state Potts antiferromagnet, H(c) = number of edges uv with c_u = c_v. Determine the ground-state energy min H. Bounds: 120 <= min H <= 134; find a colouring with at most 133 monochromatic edges, or prove 134 optimal.
submission: Text file: 120 colours 0, 1 or 2, separated by spaces or newlines, one per vertex in the checker's vertex order (the 600-cell's vertices as exact coordinates in Q(sqrt 5), sorted; see polytope_graph in checkers/orig_phys.py).
score: the number of monochromatic edges (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: simulated annealing over colourings (tools/potts.py, 6 restarts of 4,000 sweeps)

context: Potts antiferromagnets on frustrated structures (the triangular, kagome and pyrochlore lattices) are a standard source of ground-state degeneracy and order by disorder. The 600-cell, the curved-space template of icosahedral order (Nelson 1983), is maximally frustrated for them: it is made of 600 tetrahedral cells, and in any 3-colouring each cell has a monochromatic edge; since each edge lies in 5 cells, at least 120 edges are monochromatic. With 5 colours the graph can be coloured properly (our annealer finds a proper 5-colouring, and 5 is needed because every vertex neighbourhood is an icosahedron, which needs 4 colours), so the 3- and 4-state models are the frustrated ones; for 4 colours our best colouring has 66 monochromatic edges. The Ising case (2 colours) is the separate problem polytope-ising.
references: D. R. Nelson, Order, frustration, and defects in liquids and glasses, Phys. Rev. B 28 (1983) 5515
R. J. Baxter, Exactly Solved Models in Statistical Mechanics (Academic Press, 1982): Potts models
M. Waegell, P. K. Aravind et al., Critical noncolorings of the 600-cell proving the Bell-Kochen-Specker theorem, arXiv:0911.2289 (a different colouring problem on the 600-cell's rays)

novelty.verdict: new. Our arXiv searches found no paper or table on Potts antiferromagnets (or minimum monochromatic edges of colourings) of the 600-cell graph; the 600-cell colouring papers found on arXiv concern Kochen-Specker colourings of its rays, a different problem.
closest: Kochen-Specker colourings of the 600-cell's 60 rays (arXiv:0802.2533, arXiv:0911.2289): assignments to orthogonal tetrads, not vertex colourings of the polytope graph.
